teams.heading: Caleb Muntz starts at fly-half as Fiji reshuffle for Japan final
teams.body: Fly-half Caleb Muntz returns to the starting XV for Saturday’s Pacific Nations Cup final against Japan in Tokyo. Interim head coach Senirusi Seruvakula has shifted Isaiah Armstrong-Ravula to full-back to accommodate Muntz, while Elia Canakaivata replaces Isoa Tuwai at No. 8. With uncapped pair Vilikesa Nairau and Isaac Ratumaitavuki-Kneepkens named amongst the replacements, Fiji chase a third consecutive victory over the Brave Blossoms. Seruvakula noted that Japan are "a well-coached side" following their recent tests against Australia.

teams.heading: Fin Smith warns England must face hard truths if autumn form falters
teams.body: Fly-half Fin Smith has warned that any further "ropey" form this November must force the squad to have a "pretty hard look" at themselves. Despite a narrow 31-24 victory over Argentina in Round three, he told Rugby Union Weekly that the team cannot keep relying on the "building" narrative. England have managed only three wins from eight Tests in 2026, including a first-ever loss to Italy. The Northampton playmaker, who has started the last five internationals, believes the upcoming series provides a definitive test.

lead.why: Fly-half Fin Smith's candid warning about England's lack of progress is the day's most significant national storyline.

teams.heading: Ben Youngs warns France must beat South Africa to clear psychological hurdle
teams.body: Ben Youngs identifies a critical mental barrier against the Springboks that could define the 2027 World Cup prospects for Fabien Galthié’s side. Currently third in the Nations Championship, Les Bleus host the world champions in Paris this November. Speaking on the For the Love of Rugby podcast, the former England scrum-half insisted France "have to beat them" to avoid a lingering psychological hurdle. Youngs argues that after consecutive narrow home defeats, failing to win now creates a barrier the squad "cannot overcome" before Australia.

teams.heading: IRFU confirms no plans to host Six Nations games in United States
teams.body: The IRFU has rejected suggestions that any upcoming Six Nations fixtures could be moved to the United States. While World Rugby recently floated the plan to expand the sport’s commercial footprint ahead of the 2031 World Cup, the Irish union confirmed no such discussions are currently taking place. This follows reports earlier this month that England and Scotland are also hesitant to participate due to the potential loss of home matchday revenue. Any shift to North America would require unanimous support from all competing unions.

teams.heading: Italy stay silent as more Six Nations unions shun United States fixture
teams.body: Unions across the Six Nations continue to distance themselves from World Rugby's proposal to stage a championship fixture in the United States. Following reports last week that England would decline the move to protect Twickenham revenue, both the Irish and Scottish governing bodies have now clarified they have no plans to participate. While the global governing body seeks to grow the game before the 2031 World Cup, the Italian federation has yet to comment on whether the Azzurri would consider a neutral-site test.

teams.heading: Dave Butcher hands Ceitidh Ainsworth her first Scotland start against New Zealand
teams.body: Interim head coach Dave Butcher makes four changes for today’s WXV fixture against the Black Ferns at Hive Stadium. Glasgow Warriors scrum-half Ceitidh Ainsworth earns her first international start after debuting off the bench in last week’s heavy defeat by Canada. She replaces clubmate Rhea Clarke in a reshuffled backline. Experienced lock Sarah Bonar also returns to the matchday squad for the first time since the 2025 World Cup, set to earn her 52nd cap as a replacement.

teams.heading: Sean Lynn’s inspired Wales squad secure emphatic win over South Africa
teams.body: Wales returned to winning ways in emphatic fashion with a 50-19 victory over South Africa at Cardiff Arms Park. Following a nine-Test winless streak, the hosts produced an eight-try performance in their WXV Global Series opener. Coach Sean Lynn’s decision to move Keira Bevan to fly-half paid dividends as the side attacked with newfound freedom. Sisilia Tuipulotu impressed with a brace of tries, while co-captain Alex Callender made a triumphant return from injury to earn player-of-the-match honours.

teams.heading: Michael Cheika appoints Stephen Hoiles and Wycliff Palu as Waratahs assistants
teams.body: Waratahs head coach Michael Cheika has made his first backroom appointments ahead of the 2027 season, securing former Wallabies back-rowers Stephen Hoiles and Wycliff Palu on two-year deals as assistant coaches. The pair previously won the 2014 Super Rugby final together in the Waratahs' starting line-up against the Crusaders. Hoiles joins from the US club California Legion, while Palu arrives following coaching stints in Japan and with the First Nations and Pasifika XV.

teams.heading: Eddie Jones banks on experience as Japan name side for final
teams.body: Eddie Jones has recalled Faulua Makisi to start at No. 8 and brought in Tomoki Osada on the left wing as Japan named their side for Saturday's Pacific Nations Cup final against Fiji in Tokyo. Jones has selected an experienced 312-cap side, anchored by 35-cap captain Naoto Saito, 45-cap midfielder Dylan Riley and 36-cap lock Jack Cornelsen. The Brave Blossoms are chasing their first title in the competition since 2019 after suffering defeats in the previous two finals. "Our aim this weekend is to win the final and we're 100 per cent concentrated on that," Jones said.

teams.heading: John Smit examines All Blacks scrum struggles following series defeat
teams.body: Former Springboks captain John Smit believes that South Africa’s exit from Super Rugby has contributed to the All Blacks’ scrum struggles. Speaking on the I Love Rugby podcast, the 2007 World Cup-winning skipper noted that New Zealand forwards are not subjected to the same weekly set-piece examination in a competition focused heavily on attacking rugby. Smit stated, “You can train in the gym as much as you want, but if you don’t put enough time in the ring and you don’t scrum every week, and you don’t get tested by hard opposition, it’s very difficult to understand what the level is.”
